extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent prosecutors, in-house IP counsel, and patent litigators considering or handling PTAB ex parte appeals and reexaminations
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on deciding whether to appeal examiner rejections to the PTAB (ex parte), and on preparing and pursuing appeals (briefs, oral argument, rehearing), including interactions with reexamination and other post‑grant proceedings. Emphasizes timing, alternatives, and best practices from both applicant and PTAB perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal candidacy criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes a case a good candidate for appeal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider applicant perspectives including business factors, legal factors, statistics, timing, costs, and available alternative routes. Also weigh PTAB perspectives. Use these factors to decide whether appeal is appropriate for the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural alternatives applicants may use instead of or before filing an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes AFCP 2.0, Pre-Appeal Brief Request for Review, and filing an RCE. Evaluate effectiveness of each alternative in the specific case before appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: when to file an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Considerations on the proper timing to initiate an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh timing against pendency metrics, business timing, interplay with alternatives (AFCP 2.0, pre-appeal review, RCE), and strategic objectives (e.g., avoiding parallel proceedings or preserving issues for appeal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening brief quality criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: What an effective opening (appeal) brief should do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate clear arguments, rely appropriately on applicable precedent, and rely on the record evidence. Follow USPTO practice tips for writing effective briefs (see USPTO resource link). Structure and select arguments to maximize chances of reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: How to use a reply brief and what makes a good reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to file a reply based on the examiner/Board response; focus on refuting adverse points, sharpening the legal/rationale issues for reversal, and addressing any factual or evidentiary disputes. Consider strategic scope—avoid raising new issues not in the opening brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationales for reversing
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of reasoning that persuade the Board to reverse an examiner rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize legal and factual errors by the examiner, demonstrate insufficiency of prior art or incorrect application of precedent, and tie arguments to record evidence and controlling case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument: when and how
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for requesting oral argument and best practices for conducting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider factors such as the technology involved, the legal issues at stake, and costs. Understand why requests can be denied. Prepare for the process and structure of argument: decide who should argue, who should attend, the substantive content, and use of demonstratives. Balance costs and potential benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rehearing: when and how
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and best practices for seeking rehearing from the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider when to request rehearing, what issues the PTAB will consider, chances of success, and procedural handling within the Board. Use tips to improve chances (e.g., focus on clear legal errors, procedural errors, or newly identified but properly preserved issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting cases through the PTAB efficiently
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices that promote efficient and effective progress of appeals through the PTAB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt PTAB and applicant perspectives: streamline the record, choose efficient procedures (e.g., pre-appeal review where helpful), be strategic about filings and timing, and present clear, focused issues to the Board to shorten pendency and improve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations with parallel post-grant proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: How parallel post‑grant proceedings (e.g., IPR, PGR, reexamination) affect appeals and strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess impacts on procedure and potential influence on the PTAB decision; for applicants, weigh advantages (e.g., additional opportunities to challenge/defend claims) vs. risks (duplicative cost, estoppel, timing). Coordinate strategy across proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination: when and how to use it
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview and best practices for ex parte reexamination as an alternative or complement to prosecution and appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand differences from pre‑grant prosecution, review relevant statistics, consider strategic reasons to use reexamination (when to use), and follow best practices from applicant and PTAB perspectives. Consider how appeals from ex parte reexamination are handled and whether they differ procedurally or substantively from other appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal pendency metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: How pendency of appeals is measured and typical pendency data by technology area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency is calculated as average months from Board receipt date to final decision. Use pendency statistics (overall and by technology: bio/pharma, chemical, electrical/computer, design, business method/mechanical, CRU) when deciding timing and strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal intake and technology distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and distribution of appeals received by technology area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review intake numbers by technology center to understand workload and resourcing; this may inform expectations about timing and Board experience with particular technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal outcome distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical disposition percentages for appeals (affirmed, reversed, affirmed‑in‑part, remands, dismissed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY19 example: Affirmed 56.4%, Reversed 32.2%, Affirmed‑in‑part 9.3%, Administrative/panel remands 0.9%, Dismissed 1.2%. Use outcome distributions to set realistic expectations about chances of reversal.
